newsitem.title: GERMANY: Welteke happy with dlr rate, sets no goal - spokesman.
newsitem.headline: Welteke happy with dlr rate, sets no goal - spokesman.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke said on Tuesday the Bundesbank was happy with the dollar's current levels but did not wish to see the dollar move significantly higher, a state central bank spokesman said.
The spokesman for the state central bank in Hesse where Welteke is president stressed that Welteke had not mentioned any specific targets as reported by another news agency.

"(Welteke) said what he has been saying for some time and this is that the dollar's level around 1.70 marks including a few pfennigs lower or higher was not a problem," Welteke's spokesman told Reuters in answer to a query.
"But (Welteke) certainly did not give any levels at which the Bundesbank might no longer be happy with the dollar. And he certainly did not give a four digit level," the spokesman added.
One news agency had reported that Welteke had said the Bundesbank did not want the dollar to move above the 1.72 to 1.7350 marks level.
The dollar dropped by around one pfennig after the reported comments.
German officials ranging from Bundesbank officials to the economics and finance ministers generally decline to give any specific dollar levels, preferring to speak only in very general terms.
